claim: A 1,342 nm diode-pumped solid-state (DPSS) IR laser is used as the heat-shock light source in the single-cell IR-LEGO heat-shock microscope system.
source: A 1,342 nm diode-pumped solid-state (DPSS) IR laser is used as the heat-shock light source in our single-cell IR-LEGO heat-shock microscope system (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the wavelength and type of laser used in the system.

claim: The laser at 1,342 nm wavelength provides an appropriate balance between the absorption efficiency of water and penetration depth in tissue.
source: The laser at this wavelength provides an appropriate balance between the absorption efficiency of water and penetration depth in tissue (Appendix 1).
evidence: The manuscript states this balance is achieved and references Appendix 1 for supporting information.

claim: A large temperature gradient can be created in the region of about 10 µm size around the heat source.
source: A large temperature gradient can be created in the region of about 10 µm size around the heat source (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that the thermal energy produced by a highly focused IR laser heating in tissue could be confined within the single-cell dimensions for efficient single-cell gene induction.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding based on numerical simulation results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The thermal energy produced by a highly focused IR laser heating in tissue could be confined within the single-cell dimensions for efficient single-cell gene induction.
source: A large temperature gradient can be created in the region of about 10 µm size around the heat source (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that the thermal energy produced by a highly focused IR laser heating in tissue could be confined within the single-cell dimensions for efficient single-cell gene induction.
evidence: The manuscript suggests this based on the temperature gradient data from simulations.

claim: TAMRA (tetramethylrhodamine) conjugated with dextran is adopted as the probe dye in two-photon fluorescent thermometry (TPFT).
source: In details, a temperature-sensitive dye (Figure 1), tetramethylrhodamine (TAMRA) which is conjugated with dextran, is adopted as the probe dye in TPFT, while fluorescein (FITC), which is insensitive to temperature and also conjugated with dextran (Figure 1C), is used as a reference dye to eliminate the fluctuation of probe dye fluorescence caused by a variety of interferences (Appendix 3).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the use of TAMRA as the probe dye.

claim: FITC is insensitive to temperature and is used as a reference dye to eliminate the fluctuation of probe dye fluorescence caused by a variety of interferences.
source: In details, a temperature-sensitive dye (Figure 1), tetramethylrhodamine (TAMRA) which is conjugated with dextran, is adopted as the probe dye in TPFT, while fluorescein (FITC), which is insensitive to temperature and also conjugated with dextran (Figure 1C), is used as a reference dye to eliminate the fluctuation of probe dye fluorescence caused by a variety of interferences (Appendix 3).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states FITC's temperature insensitivity and its role as a reference dye.

claim: The temperature dependencies of fluorescence measured in pure TAMRA and FITC solutions are -0.882 ± 0.100%/°C and -0.165 ± 0.098%/°C respectively.
source: The temperature dependencies of fluorescence measured in pure TAMRA and FITC solutions are -0.882 ± 0.100%/°C and -0.165 ± 0.098%/°C respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2—source data 1).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific measured values with error margins and references supporting figures.

claim: The two-photon excited fluorescence (TPEF) intensity ratio of TAMRA and FITC is linearly correlated with the solution temperature due to large difference in temperature sensitivity between two dyes.
source: The two-photon excited fluorescence (TPEF) intensity ratio of TAMRA and FITC is linearly correlated with the solution temperature due to large difference in temperature sensitivity between two dyes (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript states this linear correlation and references supporting figures.

claim: The temperature sensitivities of fluorescence intensity ratio are similar in water solution, 3% agarose and zebrafish in vivo.
source: The temperature sensitivities of fluorescence intensity ratio are similar in water solution, 3% agarose and zebrafish in vivo (Figure 1D and Supplementary file 1a), indicating that the temperature coefficient of the fluorescent dextran remains stable in different environments.
evidence: The manuscript states this similarity and references supporting data.

claim: The temperature coefficient of the fluorescent dextran remains stable in different environments.
source: The temperature sensitivities of fluorescence intensity ratio are similar in water solution, 3% agarose and zebrafish in vivo (Figure 1D and Supplementary file 1a), indicating that the temperature coefficient of the fluorescent dextran remains stable in different environments.
evidence: The manuscript indicates this stability based on the similarity of temperature sensitivities across environments.

claim: There is high consistency between the actual temperature and the measured temperature using TPFT.
source: The high consistency between the actual temperature and the measured temperature (Figure 1E) demonstrates that TPFT can be used as an effective tool for in vivo measurement of the local temperature rise induced by IR laser heating in tissues.
evidence: The manuscript states this consistency and references Figure 1E showing the comparison.

claim: TPFT can be used as an effective tool for in vivo measurement of the local temperature rise induced by IR laser heating in tissues.

claim: The temperature at IR laser focal point increased sharply within 1 ~ 2 s after point heating and remained stable over the exposure time of the IR laser.
source: We found that the temperature at IR laser focal point increased sharply within 1 ~ 2 s after point heating and remained stable over the exposure time of the IR laser, before decreasing quickly to the ambient temperature as soon as the IR laser was turned off (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this temporal behavior of temperature change and references supporting figure.

claim: The temperature decreased quickly to the ambient temperature as soon as the IR laser was turned off.
source: We found that the temperature at IR laser focal point increased sharply within 1 ~ 2 s after point heating and remained stable over the exposure time of the IR laser, before decreasing quickly to the ambient temperature as soon as the IR laser was turned off (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The manuscript reports this behavior and references supporting figure.

claim: The depth of IR laser focal point in water and tissue phantom should be over 100 µm to minimize the thermal conduction at the intermedium surface.
source: The depth of IR laser focal point in water and tissue phantom should be over 100 µm to minimize the thermal conduction at the intermedium surface (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: The manuscript states this requirement and references supporting figures.

claim: High spatial resolution of heat shock could be achieved in 3% agarose.
source: Next, we measured the 3D temperature distributions (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—source data 1), and found that high spatial resolution of heat shock could be achieved in 3% agarose.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding based on 3D temperature distribution measurements.

claim: A large temperature gradient could not be built in water solution because of its high thermal conductivity and faster convection.
source: However, a large temperature gradient could not be built in water solution because of its high thermal conductivity and faster convection.
evidence: The manuscript explains why water solution does not support large temperature gradients.

claim: The thermal confinement in zebrafish muscle is higher than in tissue phantom, both laterally and axially.
source: Results showed that the thermal confinement in zebrafish muscle is higher than in tissue phantom, both laterally and axially (Figure 2C and D, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports this comparison based on in vivo measurements.

claim: The thermal conductivity of zebrafish muscle could be lower than that of 3% agarose.
source: This indicates that the thermal conductivity of zebrafish muscle could be lower than that of 3% agarose.
evidence: The manuscript infers this from the higher thermal confinement observed in zebrafish muscle.

claim: Low thermal conductivity and inefficient convection of tissue phantom plays a critical role to confine the thermal energy and achieve single-cell resolution of heat shock.
source: As shown in Figure 2 E1 and E2, low thermal conductivity and inefficient convection of tissue phantom plays a critical role to confine the thermal energy and achieve single-cell resolution of heat shock.
evidence: The manuscript states this based on 3D visualization of temperature distributions.

claim: There is no significant difference in the thermal confinement between point and scan heating methods.
source: As shown in Figure 2 E2 and E3, there is no significant difference in the thermal confinement between point and scan heating methods.
evidence: The manuscript states this comparison based on 3D temperature distribution data.

claim: TPFT can finely evaluate the thermal distribution in zebrafish muscle in vivo.
source: The results in Figure 2 E3 and E4 demonstrate that TPFT can finely evaluate the thermal distribution in zebrafish muscle in vivo and paves the way for evaluation of single-cell heat shock in different zebrafish tissues.

claim: With high IR laser power, the average temperature at the focal point (P00) of IR laser can reach as high as 50°C.
source: Using TPFT, the temperature distribution in the heat shocked tissues was measured. With high IR laser power, the average temperature at the focal point (P00) of IR laser can reach as high as 50°C (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A, Figure 2—figure supplement 4—source data 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports this measured temperature value.

claim: Considerable success rates of overall cell labeling can be achieved with high temperature heat shock, but the percentages of single-cell labeling within the overall labeling are relatively low.
source: Although considerable success rates of overall cell labeling can be achieved with this high temperature heat shock, the percentages of single-cell labeling within the overall labeling are relatively low (Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation based on experimental results.

claim: Effective heat shock gene induction can be induced with environmental temperature higher than 38°C.
source: This is due to that effective heat shock gene induction can be induced with environmental temperature higher than 38°C (Shoji and Sato-Maeda, 2008) and the heating region of temperature over 38°C was greater than the single cell size.
evidence: The manuscript cites a reference to support this temperature threshold.

claim: With the optimized heat shock condition, the temperature at 10 µm away from the focal point (P10) dropped below 38°C.
source: With the optimized heat shock condition, the temperature at 10 µm away from the focal point (P10) dropped below 38°C (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B and C, Figure 2—figure supplement 4—source data 1), preventing unwanted gene induction in neighboring cells.

claim: After heat shock with optimized laser condition, successful overall cell labeling in myocytes, neurons and leukocytes can be observed in 36.7%, 18.6% and 50% of zebrafish, respectively.
source: It was demonstrated that, after heat shock with optimized laser condition, successful overall cell labeling in myocytes, neurons and leukocytes can be observed in 36.7%, 18.6% and 50% of zebrafish, respectively, among which the efficiencies of single-cell labeling for these three types of tissues are 54.5%, 100% and 77.8%, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 4D and Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific percentages based on experimental data.

claim: The efficiencies of single-cell labeling for myocytes, neurons and leukocytes are 54.5%, 100% and 77.8%, respectively.
source: It was demonstrated that, after heat shock with optimized laser condition, successful overall cell labeling in myocytes, neurons and leukocytes can be observed in 36.7%, 18.6% and 50% of zebrafish, respectively, among which the efficiencies of single-cell labeling for these three types of tissues are 54.5%, 100% and 77.8%, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 4D and Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific percentages based on experimental data.

claim: Compared with the high-temperature heat shock, the success rates of overall cell labeling with optimized heat shock condition were decreased, but the efficiency of single-cell labeling was significantly improved.
source: Compared with the high-temperature heat shock, the success rates of overall cell labeling with optimized heat shock condition were decreased, but the efficiency of single-cell labeling was significantly improved.

claim: The single-cell IR-LEGO technology can efficiently and precisely induce heat shock-mediated gene editing within single cell in vivo in multiple tissues under optimized condition.
source: This demonstrates that the single-cell IR-LEGO technology can efficiently and precisely induce heat shock-mediated gene editing within single cell in vivo in multiple tissues under optimized condition.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the experimental results across multiple tissue types.

claim: The definitive hematopoiesis of zebrafish initiates from the HE in the ventral wall of the dorsal aorta and was thought to give rise to hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs).
source: Similar to mammals, the definitive hematopoiesis of zebrafish initiates from the HE in the ventral wall of the dorsal aorta and was thought to give rise to hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) (Bertrand et al., 2010; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010; Tian et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript states this with citations to supporting literature.

claim: The HEs in the aorta produce non-HSC progenitors capable of differentiating into T cells, myeloid and erythroid lineages but not B cells in a transient manner.
source: Yet, our recent study has shown that in addition to generating HSCs, the HEs in the aorta also produces non-HSC progenitors capable of differentiating into T cells, myeloid and erythroid lineages but not B cells in a transient manner (Tian et al., 2017; Bertrand et al., 2007), highlighting the complexity of endothelial-hematopoietic transition (EHT), a process leading to the formation of blood stem and progenitor cells from the endothelium (Bertrand et al., 2010; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010).
evidence: The manuscript cites recent studies showing this finding.

claim: The average length of endothelial cells along the aortic floor in the PBI is 24.9 µm, with the minimum of 11.2 µm.
source: Specifically, we estimated the physical sizes of HEs by measuring the distance between the nuclei of neighboring endothelial cells, and it shows that the average length of endothelial cells along the aortic floor in the PBI is 24.9 µm, with the minimum of 11.2 µm (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific measurements from experimental data.

claim: It is highly feasible to label HE at single-cell resolution using the heat-shock microscope system given that the effective heat-shock region (>38°C) can be constrained within 10 µm along the ventral wall of aorta.
source: Given that we have successfully constrained the effective heat-shock region (>38°C) within 10 µm along the ventral wall of aorta (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B and Supplementary file 1b), it is highly feasible to label HE at single-cell resolution using our heat-shock microscope system.
evidence: The manuscript infers this feasibility based on the spatial confinement achieved.

claim: GFP signal began to emerge at ~6 hrs post heat-shock and 4-OHT treatment.

claim: The high-precision single-cell IR-LEGO system can efficiently trace the progenies derived from a single HE with high fidelity.

source: As a strategy for cell labeling and tracing, our single-cell IR-LEGO technique can be applied on any cell type as long as the IR laser can penetrate through the tissues above the targeted cells.

claim: HEs in the PBI directly give rise to at least two distinct hematopoietic precursors: one capable of generating both T lymphocytes and myeloid cells and the other producing myeloid cells only.

source: Given the fact that the erythroid-myeloid and lymphoid-myeloid progenitors but not lymphoid-erythroid progenitors have been identified in both mouse and zebrafish (Bertrand et al., 2007; Perdiguero and Geissmann, 2016; McGrath et al., 2015; Böiers et al., 2013), we attend to speculate that the HEs in the PBI may likely give rise to two different progenitor populations with lymphoid-myeloid potential and erythroid-myeloid potential respectively (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies showing this.

claim: The HEs in the PBI may likely give rise to two different progenitor populations with lymphoid-myeloid potential and erythroid-myeloid potential respectively.
source: Given the fact that the erythroid-myeloid and lymphoid-myeloid progenitors but not lymphoid-erythroid progenitors have been identified in both mouse and zebrafish (Bertrand et al., 2007; Perdiguero and Geissmann, 2016; McGrath et al., 2015; Böiers et al., 2013), we attend to speculate that the HEs in the PBI may likely give rise to two different progenitor populations with lymphoid-myeloid potential and erythroid-myeloid potential respectively (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript speculates this based on known progenitor types.

claim: Studies in mice suggested that erythro-myeloid progenitors (EMPs) and HSCs are derived from distinct subpopulations of endothelial cells.
source: Studies in mice suggested that erythro-myeloid progenitors (EMPs) and HSCs are derived from distinct subpopulations of endothelial cells (Chen et al., 2011), and the mammalian HSCs showed heterogeneity during their emergence from the E11 AGM in mid-gestation embryos (Ye et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies in mice showing this.

claim: Mammalian HSCs showed heterogeneity during their emergence from the E11 AGM in mid-gestation embryos.
source: Studies in mice suggested that erythro-myeloid progenitors (EMPs) and HSCs are derived from distinct subpopulations of endothelial cells (Chen et al., 2011), and the mammalian HSCs showed heterogeneity during their emergence from the E11 AGM in mid-gestation embryos (Ye et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites a study showing this heterogeneity.

claim: The generation of HSC-independent hematopoietic cells via EHT occurs in both PBI and AGM in zebrafish.
source: In addition, our previous study has demonstrated that the generation of HSC-independent hematopoietic cells via EHT occurs in both PBI and AGM in zebrafish (Tian et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites a previous study demonstrating this.

claim: The heterogeneity of HEs is not a phenomenon restricted in the PBI region but broadly exists along the aortic floor.
source: Taken together, these studies raise the possibility that the heterogeneity of HEs is not a phenomenon restricted in the PBI region but broadly exists along the aortic floor (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript raises this possibility based on multiple cited studies.

claim: Studies in both mammals and zebrafish showed that new-born HSPCs dynamically interact with different cell types in various microenvironments, which is important for the migration, maintenance, proliferation and function of HSPCs.
source: Indeed, studies in both mammals and zebrafish showed that new-born HSPCs dynamically interact with different cell types in various microenvironments, which is important for the migration, maintenance, proliferation and function of HSPCs (Tamplin et al., 2015; Gao et al., 2018; Li et al., 2018), and perhaps, is also crucial for lineage commitment.
evidence: The manuscript cites studies showing these interactions and their importance.

claim: The interactions between hematopoietic progenitors and niches may be crucial for lineage commitment.
source: Indeed, studies in both mammals and zebrafish showed that new-born HSPCs dynamically interact with different cell types in various microenvironments, which is important for the migration, maintenance, proliferation and function of HSPCs (Tamplin et al., 2015; Gao et al., 2018; Li et al., 2018), and perhaps, is also crucial for lineage commitment.
evidence: The manuscript speculates this based on the known importance of niche interactions.

claim: Heterogeneity broadly exists in various cell types both during development and at homeostasis.
source: Heterogeneity broadly exists in various cell types both during development and at homeostasis.
evidence: The manuscript states this in the abstract as a general principle.

claim: Investigating heterogeneity is crucial for comprehensively understanding the complexity of ontogeny, dynamics, and function of specific cell types.
source: Investigating heterogeneity is crucial for comprehensively understanding the complexity of ontogeny, dynamics, and function of specific cell types.
evidence: The manuscript states this importance in the abstract.

claim: Traditional bulk-labeling techniques are incompetent to dissect heterogeneity within cell population.
source: Traditional bulk-labeling techniques are incompetent to dissect heterogeneity within cell population, while the new single-cell lineage tracing methodologies invented in the last decade can hardly achieve high-fidelity single-cell labeling and long-term in-vivo observation simultaneously.
evidence: The manuscript states this limitation of traditional techniques.

claim: New single-cell lineage tracing methodologies invented in the last decade can hardly achieve high-fidelity single-cell labeling and long-term in-vivo observation simultaneously.
source: Traditional bulk-labeling techniques are incompetent to dissect heterogeneity within cell population, while the new single-cell lineage tracing methodologies invented in the last decade can hardly achieve high-fidelity single-cell labeling and long-term in-vivo observation simultaneously.
evidence: The manuscript states this limitation of newer techniques.

claim: The developed system uses laser-induced CreERT2 combined with loxP-DsRedx-loxP-GFP reporter to achieve precise single-cell labeling and tracing.
source: In this work, we developed a high-precision infrared laser-evoked gene operator heat-shock system, which uses laser-induced CreERT2 combined with loxP-DsRedx-loxP-GFP reporter to achieve precise single-cell labeling and tracing.
evidence: The manuscript describes the system developed in this work.

claim: The system can precisely label single cell in brain, muscle and hematopoietic system in zebrafish embryo.
source: In vivo study indicated that this system can precisely label single cell in brain, muscle and hematopoietic system in zebrafish embryo.
evidence: The manuscript states this capability demonstrated in vivo.

claim: HEs in the PBI are heterogeneous, which contains at least myeloid unipotent and myeloid-lymphoid bipotent subtypes.
source: Using this system, we traced the hematopoietic potential of hemogenic endothelium (HE) in the posterior blood island (PBI) of zebrafish embryo and found that HEs in the PBI are heterogeneous, which contains at least myeloid unipotent and myeloid-lymphoid bipotent subtypes.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding from the lineage tracing study.

claim: Zebrafish has natural advantages on hematopoietic fate mapping owing to the external development, transparent embryo body and its highly conserved hematopoiesis.
source: Zebrafish has natural advantages on hematopoietic fate mapping owing to the external development, transparent embryo body and its highly conserved hematopoiesis (Jagannathan-Bogdan and Zon, 2013; Stachura and Traver, 2016).
evidence: The manuscript states these advantages and cites supporting references.

claim: Permanent genetic marking, photo-convertible labeling and in vivo time-lapse imaging have been employed to monitor the generation, mobilization and lineage specification of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs) in zebrafish.
source: Taking these advantages, permanent genetic marking, photo-convertible labeling and in vivo time-lapse imaging have been employed to monitor the generation, mobilization and lineage specification of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs) in zebrafish (Murayama et al., 2006; Jin et al., 2007; Bertrand et al., 2010; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies that have used these techniques.

claim: The infrared laser-evoked gene operator (IR-LEGO) microscope heating system has been demonstrated as a powerful tool for bulk cell tracing with high temporal-spatial resolution.
source: Recently, the infrared laser-evoked gene operator (IR-LEGO) microscope heating system (Deguchi, 2009; Kamei et al., 2009) has been demonstrated as a powerful tool for bulk cell tracing with high temporal-spatial resolution (Shimada et al., 2013; Okuyama et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2015; Tian et al., 2017; Singhal and Shaham, 2017; He et al., 2018; Henninger et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies demonstrating this capability.

claim: In the IR-LEGO system, an infrared (IR) laser is used to generate local heat shock to induce CreER expression in a restricted region of transgenic fish.
source: In this system, an infrared (IR) laser is used to generate local heat shock to induce CreER expression in a restricted region of transgenic fish carrying a tissue-specific loxP-DsRedx-loxP-GFP reporter and a hsp70l:mCherry-T2a-CreERT2.
evidence: The manuscript describes how the IR-LEGO system works.

claim: The removal of DsRedx cassette is permanently inherited so that the progenies derived from the targeted tissue will display GFP instead of DsRedx.
source: The removal of DsRedx cassette is permanently inherited so that the progenies derived from the targeted tissue will display GFP instead of DsRedx (Xu et al., 2015; Tian et al., 2017; He et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript explains the genetic mechanism and cites supporting studies.

claim: Heterogeneity broadly exists in multiple cell populations during hematopoiesis.
source: However, it has been realized that heterogeneity broadly exists in multiple cell populations during hematopoiesis (Tian et al., 2017; Wilson et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2011; Crisan and Dzierzak, 2016; Ye et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple studies showing this heterogeneity.

claim: The dissection of heterogeneity requires a lineage tracing strategy with single cell resolution.
source: The dissection of heterogeneity requires a lineage tracing strategy with single cell resolution.
evidence: The manuscript states this requirement for studying heterogeneity.

claim: Previous IR-LEGO techniques face fundamental challenges including high-precision and efficient labeling of the targeted single cell.
source: Yet, the previous IR-LEGO techniques (Deguchi, 2009; Kamei et al., 2009; Shimada et al., 2013; Okuyama et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2015; Tian et al., 2017; Singhal and Shaham, 2017; He et al., 2018; Kawasumi‐Kita, 2015; Suzuki et al., 2014; Eiji, 2013; Hayashi et al., 2014; Miao and Hayashi, 2015; Hasugata et al., 2018) face the following fundamental challenges: (1) high-precision and efficient labeling of the targeted single cell; (2) fine balance between labeling efficiency and cell viability after heat shock treatment; (3) permanent marking and long-term tracing of all progeny of the labeled single cell; (4) rigorous statistical analysis to quantitatively determine the lineages of the labeled single cell under random basal interference.
evidence: The manuscript lists challenges faced by previous techniques and cites relevant studies.

claim: It remains unclear whether IR-LEGO technique can indeed be used for long-term tracing of multiple lineages of a single multipotent cell, such as HSPC.
source: These challenges hamper the wider application of IR-LEGO for cell fate mapping, and it remains unclear whether this technique can indeed be used for long-term tracing of multiple lineages of a single multipotent cell, such as HSPC.
evidence: The manuscript states this uncertainty about the technique's capability.

claim: Cell barcode techniques have been used to perform single-cell lineage tracing in hematopoiesis studies.
source: Cell barcode techniques, either by retroviral library infection to insert inheritable DNA barcodes (Naik et al., 2014), or by CRISPR/Cas9 system to accumulate random mutations (McKenna et al., 2016; Kalhor et al., 2017), have been used to perform single-cell lineage tracing in hematopoiesis studies (Gerrits et al., 2010; Lu et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites studies using these techniques.

claim: Non-imaging based techniques like cell barcoding are not suitable for tracing the dynamic behaviors of the targeted cells and their progenies.
source: However, these non-imaging based techniques are not suitable for tracing the dynamic behaviors of the targeted cells and their progenies.
evidence: The manuscript states this limitation of non-imaging techniques.

claim: A multicolor strategy has been utilized for cell fate mapping by stochastically expressing multiple fluorescent reporters in target cells via Cre-mediated recombination.
source: A multicolor strategy, which stochastically expresses multiple fluorescent reporters in target cells via Cre-mediated recombination, forming dozens of different color modes to distinguish individual cells and their progenies, has been utilized for cell fate mapping (Livet et al., 2007; Cai et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript describes this strategy and cites relevant studies.

claim: Multicolor labeling of cells makes it difficult to directly visualize the development of individual cell lineage.
source: Despite its success in some zebrafish hematopoiesis study (Henninger et al., 2017; Pan et al., 2013), this multicolor labeling of cells makes it difficult to directly visualize the development of individual cell lineage.
evidence: The manuscript states this limitation of multicolor labeling.

claim: The lineage hierarchy could be misinterpreted when unrelated cells share the same color or Cre-mediated recombination occurs in the daughter cells.
source: In addition, the lineage hierarchy could be misinterpreted when unrelated cells share the same color or Cre-mediated recombination occurs in the daughter cells.
evidence: The manuscript states this potential for misinterpretation.

claim: Photo-convertible protein or caged fluorescent dyes approaches have limitation for long-term tracing due to the self-degradation and rapid dilution of fluorophores during cell division.
source: Likewise, photo-convertible protein or caged fluorescent dyes approaches also have limitation for long-term tracing due to the self-degradation and rapid dilution of fluorophores during cell division (Tian et al., 2017; Warga et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript states this limitation and cites supporting studies.

claim: The basal uncaging level of the caged compound in zebrafish embryo was as high as 28%.
source: However, the basal uncaging level of the caged compound in zebrafish embryo was as high as 28% (Sinha et al., 2010b), limiting the application of this technique to trace the long-term development of highly dynamic cells, such as stem cells.
evidence: The manuscript cites a study reporting this high basal uncaging level.

claim: Developing a highly precise single-cell labeling method for the long-term in vivo tracing of individual cells will be important for understanding the heterogeneity of HSPCs.
source: Thus, developing a highly precise single-cell labeling method for the long-term in vivo tracing of individual cells will be important for understanding the heterogeneity of HSPCs.
evidence: The manuscript states this importance based on the limitations of existing techniques.

claim: A two-photon fluorescent thermometer is utilized to measure the temperature rise in vivo to achieve precise single-cell labeling.
source: To overcome the drawbacks of existing techniques, we develop a high-precision single-cell IR-LEGO technology, in which a two-photon fluorescent thermometer is utilized to measure the temperature rise in vivo to achieve precise single-cell labeling.
evidence: The manuscript describes the key innovation of the developed technology.

claim: The high-precision single-cell IR-LEGO technology has outstanding capacity to perform single-cell labeling and long-term in-vivo lineage tracing.
source: Our study demonstrates that the high-precision single-cell IR-LEGO technology has outstanding capacity to perform single-cell labeling and long-term in-vivo lineage tracing.
evidence: The manuscript concludes this based on the study results.

claim: The majority of coro1a+ cells (86.2%) on the trunk are lyz+ or mpeg1+ myeloid cells.
source: The colocalization percentages of mpeg1+/coro1a+ and lyz+/coro1a+ cells are 59.9% and 26.3%, respectively (n = 3), while lyz+ cells are not colocalized with mpeg+ cells, indicating that the majority of coro1a+ cells (86.2%) on the trunk are lyz+ or mpeg1+ myeloid cells.
